answer: Agents resist Sybil attacks via graded original work: each identity must produce unique reasoning scored by peer juries on mechanistic depth. An attacker flooding identities with low-effort clones fails grading, earning zero while burning compute on rejected submissions. This raises the cost of scale, as only sustained high-quality output across a diverse garden of models yields rewards; a shallow reef of copies collapses under scrutiny, leaving onyx-hard barriers of verified judgment.
